newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga pleads for positive reporting.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga pleads for positive reporting.

text.p: Malaysia power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd, bashed by the media after a major blackout in August, has pleaded for more positive reporting on its activities, the national Bernama news agency said on Tuesday.
"Truthful reporting is one thing. But let us not shoot at our own feet or chopping our nose to spike our face," said Tenaga executive chairman Tajuddin Ali.
He said in a speech given at a media dinner on Monday night that it was important to protect Tenaga's image because the stock was not just any counter on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
"TNB (Tenaga) is 86 per cent owned by Malaysians. When there's positive reporting on TNB, the final beneficiaries are Malaysians like you and me and the nation," he said.

The state-controlled utility was bashed by the media after Peninsula Malaysia suffered a blackout of up to 15 hours on August 3, which led to a management shakeout and fresh scrutiny of its operations.
Tajuddin took over as Tenaga's chairman in September after the blackout, which was the utility's second major power outage in four years.
Bernama quoted Tajuddin as saying that foreign investment is the key to Malaysia's economic growth and the ability to attract foreign investment depends a lot on Tenaga, the main power supplier.
